name: What warranty should I expect with cabinet refacing, and what usually is not covered?

mainEntity.name: What warranty should I expect with cabinet refacing, and what usually is not covered?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A warranty should clearly identify the covered materials, installation work, finish defects, hardware, exclusions, claim process, and duration. A warranty may not cover damage from leaks, misuse, harsh cleaners, normal wear, or movement in an unsound existing box.

Context: Refacing uses existing structures, so coverage can differ between new doors and retained cabinet boxes. Verbal assurances are difficult to evaluate after the project is complete.

Key factors:
- Whether the warranty covers labor as well as materials.
- Requirements for reporting defects and maintaining finishes.
- Treatment of pre-existing damage and products supplied by the homeowner.

Practical guidance: Request the warranty before signing, and keep product names, finish samples, invoices, and completion photos. Ask who handles adjustments if doors rub or drawers become misaligned.

Elite Remodeling & Design can clarify the project scope and post-installation responsibilities before cabinet work begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask for written coverage of materials, labor, finishes, hardware, defects, adjustments, exclusions, and the claim process. Existing-box damage, leaks, misuse, harsh cleaners, and normal wear may be excluded. Keep the warranty with product information and final project photos.
